pageCache.text:
SUCCESS through our endeavours
Nigel Armsby BA (Hons), PGCE, MA, NPQH
Welcome to Highams Park School, a mixed 11-18 comprehensive school that serves its local community, with over 1600 students on roll, comprising of 240 students in each year group from Years 7 - 11, and approximately 350 students in our Sixth Form. The legal status of the school is a Single Academy Trust, an independent state funded school.
Our school motto of “Success through our Endeavours” coupled with our core behaviours of Respect, Responsibility and Resilience sum up the importance of the development of students' character alongside our role of delivering academic excellence. A strong relationship between students, their parents/carers, and the school is vital in ensuring students fulfil their potential. Our hope is that students who join Highams Park School in Year 7 are at the start of a seven-year journey, remaining with us until the end of Year 13, when they will progress onto the next phase of their life and enter employment, or continue their studies at University.

pageCache.pageTitle: Highams Park School - Ethos & Core Values
pageCache.text:
Ethos & Core Values
Introduction to the school
Highams Park School is a mixed 11-18 comprehensive school serving the local area. As an Academy it is run by Highams Park Academy Trust. The Trust is the equivalent of the Governing Body for the school. Unlike sponsored Academies that are part of a chain, Highams Park Academy Trust only exists to support Highams Park School.
The Trustees are also the directors of Highams Park Academy Trust and appoint all the school staff and make all strategic policy decisions for the school. Most of them have a long association with the school; many are parents of current or former students of the school and all share your ambition to see the students reach their potential.
There are over 1,600 students, including approximately 350 in the 6th Form. The school is very popular and heavily oversubscribed. Students regularly achieve excellent exam results both at GCSE and A level. The majority of students continue into the 6th Form and go on to University and higher education, some to the most prestigious institutions in the country.
As an Academy, we are funded directly by the Government and hold true to our core values. These define the principles used to make decisions throughout the school and it is our ambition for all families to adopt them as something that they contribute to, rather than anything that is imposed upon them. The school’s motto of “Success through our Endeavours”, summarises these values and reflects our belief that it is by collective hard work that future success is achieved.
The school seeks to produce good citizens so we expect students to help build a calm but purposeful atmosphere with a clearly defined pattern of behaviour and dress. Considerable emphasis is placed on developing caring and considerate attitudes in our students. The core behaviours of “Respect, Responsibility and Resilience” underpin all school rules and expectations. We recognise the value of the individual and make every effort to provide opportunities for children to succeed, not only in academic work, but also in every aspect of life. We have high expectations and we organise a rigorous curriculum to stretch every student. Children’s progress is carefully monitored and reported regularly to parents. The curriculum is carefully constructed to prepare children for the world, equipped with the relevant attitudes, skills and qualifications.
Homework is organised for all students, which takes account of their age and ability. Tasks are set to do at home which may include assignments and investigative work as well as more traditional homework tasks. Microsoft Teams – the school’s digital learning resource, is used extensively to support learning.
The Pastoral System is organised in such a way that, as far as possible, parents have contact throughout the five years with one Tutor who will know their child’s character. Any parent is welcome to discuss a problem with the Tutor or the Head of Year as appropriate.
Many extra-curricular activities are organised by staff. These include participation in sport, drama, music and a variety of clubs. These take place before school, at lunchtime, after school and at weekends. There are also opportunities for the children to participate in residential courses, fieldwork and educational visits.
We are extremely proud of our students’ achievements and the facilities available for them. However, students’ achievements are made possible through their own dedicated hard work alongside the support and guidance of the high calibre teachers, support staff and trustees that we are lucky to have at Highams Park School.
Core Values
The core values expressed below sum up the spirit of the school
We aim to:
Ensure equality of opportunity for all;
Mission statement
At Highams Park we all work together to ensure all students and staff have the opportunity to achieve their personal best both educationally and morally. We aim to enable students to have responsibility for taking their place successfully in a diverse and ever changing society. We encourage and promote mutual respect for each other, hard work and personal resilience all set within a stimulating educational environment.
This vision is captured in the school motto:
‘Success through our endeavours’

pageCache.pageTitle: Highams Park School - Welcome to Year 7
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Year 7
We are excited to welcome you to Highams Park School and are thrilled that you are joining us in Year 7.
We are aware from previous years that the move from Year 6 into Year 7 can sometimes feel like a huge responsibility for the students and for you as a parent. We aim to make the transition from Primary to Secondary school as smooth and as stress free as possible. Our designated transition co-ordinator Mrs Hickman oversees the transition programme over the summer term to ensure we learn as much as we can about each student to enable them to settle quickly and flourish in September. The Year 7 coordinator Mrs Hickman works closely with the Year 7 form tutors and Head of Year along with the new students.
Our transition programme starts as soon as the student is offered a place here at Highams Park School to make sure students have the opportunity to become familiar and comfortable within the school before they start with us in September. We look forward to meeting you in person, and working with you in the next coming months.
First day of School – 3rd September 2025
First day of school: arrive by 8.30am via the student entrance at the end of Beverley Road (off Hale End Road). Parents, if you are dropping your child at school, please ensure you leave them at the end of Beverley Road to make their own way to the gate. Beverley Road is a residential street with a dead end at the school gate and there is no availability to turn a vehicle around.
Students should be in full school uniform and should have all the necessary equipment (pens, pencils, calculator, rubber, ruler, sharpener). We will be taking fingerprints in the morning so as long as you have set up your Arbor parent account and transferred some funds to your child's canteen account then they will be able to use the canteen on the first day. Or feel free to send them with a packed lunch if you prefer.
Only our new year 7s and new year 12s will be in school on this day which will enable the new students to experience a school day before the remainder of the school start back on Thursday.
If your child is not able to attend on this day or any other day, please report their absence via the 'Parents' tab on the school website. You must do this every day that they are absent and please follow this link if your child needs to leave during the school day for an appointment etc.
School finishes at 3.15pm.

Welcome
We are delighted that you are considering joining Highams Park 6th Form. Should you be successful in your application you will join the school at a very exciting time. Not only will you be taught by a well-established and experienced group of staff, but our 6th Form will provide you with a challenging and highly professional experience that is proudly the pinnacle of the school.
Ofsted
Our Sixth Form has been judged to be Outstanding following a rigorous inspection process on 22nd and 23rd May 2024. This outcome is testament to the high-quality provision that is on offer in our Sixth Form, and the dedication of both our staff and students in ensuring that teaching, learning and enrichment opportunities are consistently of the highest calibre.
The OFSTED report highlights the exceptional educational and personal development opportunities that are on offer to our students in the Sixth Form, that make our establishment such a positive and unique environment for students to study in for their Post-16 educational journey:
Results
Our Key Stage 5 results since the academic year of 2018/19 have been excellent, both our A Level and Level 3 BTEC results placed Highams Park School within the top 25% of Post-16 education providers nationally for student progress during this time. In 2025 we were placed in the top 15% of the country for progress in A level and 10% at BTEC. This led to us being awarded a Gold Award by ALPs for outstanding student process.
Three key factors behind these outstanding results are firstly, the hard working and dedicated nature of the students who join our 6th Form; secondly, our highly experienced teaching staff who are all specialists in their subjects; and thirdly, our purpose built 6th Form facilities, that includes dedicated 6th Form classrooms and 3 separate 6th Form study areas, supporting our students in becoming independent learners.
Support
Students are supported to quickly develop the skills and attitude to adjust to life in our Sixth Form. The transition from year 11 into year 12 is strategically planned and delivered by our supportive and highly knowledgeable Sixth Form team. In this stimulating and rewarding environment, our students become confident and well-rounded young people, prepared for adult life. Throughout your time in the Sixth Form, students will be able to experience our extensive careers and enrichment programme, which will enable them to develop both personally and academically.
Through a rigorous and broad academic and pastoral support programme, the Sixth Form maintains high standards to ensure that each student can flourish in our Sixth Form and beyond. ​
As a 6th Form student at Highams Park School you will be valued, challenged and nurtured, leaving better prepared to take your next step, whether that is progressing onto higher education, or entering employment.
Head of 6th Form (ID 1313)
Mr N Armsby
Ms S Awan

Our school motto, “Success through our Endeavours,” summarises these values and reflects our belief that future success is achieved through collective hard work, commitment, and consistent effort.

Super Curriculum
As part of a job application or the university application process, every applicant must write a personal statement. It's a chance for you to articulate why you'd like to study a particular course or subject, or why you feel you would be suitable for a job, and what skills and experience you possess that show your passion for your chosen field. You want to make sure that your personal statement stands out from the crowd, and the best way to demonstrate your enthusiasm and passion for your subject is by taking part in super curriculum activities.
Throughout school you will have the opportunity to, mentor younger students, be part of a variety of clubs and societies, plus much more….However, you should also be undertaking your own super curriculum activities to really make an impression. You can even start doing this as early as year 7!
Activities could include reading around your subject, listening to podcasts, or attending open lectures.
Start recording everything you are doing, so you don't forget - you'll need it for your CV and your personal statement.

pageCache.pageTitle: Highams Park School - Student Spotlight   Regan Anderson
pageCache.text:
Student Spotlight - Regan Anderson
We are incredibly proud to celebrate the achievement of Regan Anderson, who was selected to play for Millwall's First Team in their Carabao Cup match against Newcastle United on Tuesday 8th September.
To be chosen to represent a Championship club at first-team level at the age of 15 years old is a fantastic accomplishment and reflects the dedication, hard work, and talent that he has shown throughout his football journey.
What makes this achievement even more commendable is his commitment to his education. Despite having such an important fixture, he attended school before the match, demonstrating excellent maturity, professionalism, and dedication to his studies alongside his sporting commitments.
The match finished with a 1-0 victory for Newcastle United, with the game's only goal scored by Joe Willock. This result provided an interesting connection to our school community, as Joe Willock is a former Highams Park School student who has gone on to enjoy a successful professional football career at the highest level. Seeing both a former and current Highams Park student involved in the same high-profile fixture is something the whole school community can be proud of.
Everyone at Highams Park School congratulates Regan on this outstanding achievement. We look forward to following his progress and wish him every success as he continues to develop both on the pitch and in the classroom.
Mrs Woods - Learning Centre Manager

Highams Park Celebrates Another Year of GCSE Success
Following on from the strong results that were achieved last week by Year 13 students, Highams Park is very pleased that Year 11 students continue to achieve very good results in their Level 2 qualifications. Every headline measure for the year group showed an improvement on the last academic year, with our attainment 8 score rising from 47.76 to 48.83, and the number of students achieving at least a grade 4 in English and Maths increasing from 68% to 71%. Furthermore, 71% of GCSEs on the whole were awarded at least a grade 4, another increase on percentages from last year. This highlights the hard work and commitment that our students have shown to achieve such positive outcomes.
Overall, 515 grades were recorded at 9-7 received across the Year 11 cohort this year, which is an outstanding achievement for our students. 26 students received grades which averaged as a 7, with students like Arthur, Adem, Roberto and Cliodhna all achieving an average grade of an 8 overall. In addition, the BTEC qualifications undertaken at Highams Park also had very strong results, with students such as Nithusha, Olivia, Rachel and Safiya getting the top Distinction grades in Health and Social Care. Subjects like Drama, Art and Mathematics also gained outstanding outcomes, with over 75% of students getting at least a grade 5 or above. This highlights the depth of the curriculum on offer and the wide variety of different pathways that students can take during their studies at Highams Park. The vast range of subjects that students achieved these top grades shows the depth of high-quality teaching that students experienced at Highams Park.
All of our students who have achieved above their targets deserve praise for their achievements, which come from a combination of student self-discipline, strong parental support and dedicated teacher input throughout their secondary school careers. In addition, we were very pleased to welcome our local councillors Rosalind Dore and Tony Bell into school to celebrate these excellent achievements with our students. They were very pleased to hear all about the successes of our students and the strong results that they had achieved.
Nigel Armsby, Principal of Highams Park School was extremely impressed with the results achieved by the Year 11 cohort and said that “Our Year 11 students have once again achieved extremely impressive results across their subjects. We are continuously proud of the hard work that our students put in to ensure that they are making expected progress. Their dedication and resilience are admirable, and it is pleasing that so many students are continuing onto their first-choice post-16 destination, with a majority choosing to stay at Highams Park for Sixth Form”.
As a result of the excellent results achieved by Year 11, Highams Park is very pleased that a majority of their Year 11 students have chosen to remain at our outstanding Sixth Form for their A level and BTEC Level 3 studies. It was great that the number choosing to enrol in the Sixth Form was high, with 230 students at present choosing to study at Highams Park for their Level 3 studies. This is in addition to many students from other schools both within and beyond Waltham Forest choosing to come to Highams Park to experience the broad curriculum that is on offer in the Sixth Form.
